content.text: Quantum entanglement is a phenomenon in quantum mechanics where two or more particles become correlated in such a way that the quantum state of each particle cannot be described independently of the others, even when separated by large distances. When a measurement is performed on one entangled particle, the result instantaneously determines the corresponding property of its partner particle — regardless of the distance between them. Einstein famously called this 'spooky action at a distance' and was deeply skeptical of it, but it has since been confirmed experimentally many times. Entanglement is a key resource in quantum computing, quantum cryptography, and quantum teleportation.
